readSections: complete technical body including normals encoding and stone-wall lighting examples
supports: normal map stores direction data rather than surface colour
fine bumps and grooves can affect lighting without added fine mesh detail
Unity Y+ convention; neutral uncompressed RGB approximately128,128,255

facts: Each texel stores a direction, not the visible material colour.
For standard unsigned RGB tangent-space encoding, rgb=(normal+1)/2 and normal=2rgb-1.
Neutral tangent normal(0,0,1) is encoded(.5,.5,1), approximately8bit(128,128,255); blue-purple is encoded data.
limits: Tangent-space axes use surfaceU,V,outward, not worldXYZ.
Ordinary unsigned textures need the mapping; floating-point signed textures are a different storage option.
8-bit128 is quantized approximation to.5; imported/compressed GPU representations may differ.

supports: normal means the perpendicular surface direction
shading normals can vary while mesh vertices stay fixed

sourceParagraphMap.fact: Basic pixel-art sheet guides simple3Dmesh+skeleton in3dsMax; low in-game pixel height makes dense modelling unnecessary.
In-house tool renders low resolution with no antialiasing; pose-to-pose keys and carefully placed intermediate frames shape attacks.
Each animation frame exports PNG plus its normal map for a basic toon shader.
Retiming poses, adding armour and reusing models/animations reduce rework.
Lighting and pixelation tools addressed hand-drawn shading workload; flickering pixels/detail were explicit tradeoffs.
